definition: Stance detection, also known as stance classification, is a task in natural language processing (NLP) and computational linguistics that uses content analysis and text mining to identify an author's position or stance on a specific subject.
details: The task is most commonly framed as a classification or textual entailment problem over a fixed label set. Applications of stance detection include political discourse analysis, public health monitoring, misinformation identification, and content moderation on social media. Research interest in the task grew after the release of the SemEval-2016 Task 6 benchmark, the first standardized dataset for stance detection on social media, which established shared evaluation norms for the NLP community. Although historically conflated with sentiment analysis, stance detection has increasingly been recognized as a distinct task of argument mining and opinion mining within NLP. Methodological approaches have included traditional machine learning and deep learning architectures, as well as large language models due to their ability to generalize across targets and domains.

explainer.lead: Stance detection identifies an author's position on a specific subject using content analysis and text mining. It matters for applications such as political discourse analysis, public health monitoring, misinformation identification, and content moderation.

tiers.eli5: It's figuring out not just what someone is talking about, but which side they're on—like telling whether a review is for or against a product.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers usually frame it as classification or textual entailment over a fixed label set. A pitfall is that stance depends on the target, so the same text can take different stances toward different subjects.
tiers.paperLevel: An NLP and computational-linguistics task, also called stance classification, most commonly framed as classification or textual entailment over a fixed label set; research interest grew after the SemEval-2016 Task 6 benchmark, the first standardized social-media stance dataset.

explainer.example: For the target 'recycling', the text 'It's a waste of everyone's time' is labeled as opposing the target rather than neutral.
